LESSON: WRITING 12.4.1 FUNCTIONAL WRITING

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 12
Topic 12.4: Writing 12.4.1 Functional Writing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 12.4.1 Functional Writing, part of Strand 12 in Grade 6 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: Why do we keep journals and diaries? 2. How do you record important occasions or dates in your life?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. identify all the components of a personal journal,

2. read a sample personal journal,

3. create a personal journal for seven days,

4. peer-edit the personal journals, different pairs exchange their journals for editing,

5. revise personal journals,

6. display the personal journals in class. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. identify all the components of a personal journal,
2. read a sample personal journal,
3. create a personal journal for seven days,
4. peer-edit the personal journals, different pairs exchange their journals for editing,
5. revise personal journals,
6. display the personal journals in class. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 12.4.1 Functional Writing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Creativity and Imagination: The learner’s ability to undertake tasks that require artistic expression is enhanced as

they create a personal journal for seven days.

• Self-efficacy: The learner’s ability to confidently communicate is developed as they become more adept at creating

personal journals.

109

Values:
• Responsibility: This is fostered as the learner carries out assigned tasks as they create personal journals and share

them with peers.

• Social justice: It is displayed as the learner acquires a sense of sharing resources equitably as they interact with

information on environmental conservation.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Life Skills (Effective communication): The learner is able to communicate clearly as they practise creating a personal

journal for seven days.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner is able to relate the concept of making and keeping a journal to self-assessment when learning Social

Studies.
